message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The fundamentals support a modest long position: total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% from $383.3 billion), operating income of $123.2 billion, net income of $93.7 billion, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion — a business generating roughly $118 billion of annual operating cash while returning $95.0 billion via buybacks and $15.2 billion in dividends. Growth was led by Services (+13% to $96.2 billion, with 73.9% gross margin) and total gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%, though I noted the offsets: iPhone flat at $201.2 billion, Greater China down 8% to $67.0 billion, and a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge from the EU State Aid Decision that pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% and net income below the prior year. With the quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed one buy limit order for 40 shares at $223.00 — a limit essentially at market, ~$8,920 notional, comfortably under the $10,000 per-order cap and the only trade today, so well within the $20,000 daily limit. The order filled at $223.00 for $8,920, funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance (no money left the account), and the account now holds 40 AAPL shares alongside the existing 100 MSFT shares.
message.reasoning:
Order filled at 223.00, 40 shares = $8,920. Under $10k per order, total today $8,920 < $20,000. Cash was $50,000, so no money moved out.

Summary paragraph.
